claim: The dendrites of starburst amacrine cells (SACs) in the mammalian retina are preferentially activated by motion in the centrifugal direction.
source: The dendrites of starburst amacrine cells (SACs) in the mammalian retina are preferentially activated by motion in the centrifugal direction, a property that is important for generating direction selectivity in direction selective ganglion cells (DSGCs).
evidence: This is a well-established finding in the field, supported by citations throughout the manuscript (Euler et al., 2002).

claim: Centrifugal direction selectivity of SAC dendrites is important for generating direction selectivity in direction selective ganglion cells (DSGCs).
source: The dendrites of starburst amacrine cells (SACs) in the mammalian retina are preferentially activated by motion in the centrifugal direction, a property that is important for generating direction selectivity in direction selective ganglion cells (DSGCs).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental results showing that impaired SAC direction selectivity leads to impaired DSGC direction selectivity.

claim: Lateral inhibition onto Off SACs from non-SAC amacrine cells is required for optimal direction selectivity of the Off pathway.
source: We found that lateral inhibition onto Off SACs from non-SAC amacrine cells is required for optimal direction selectivity of the Off pathway.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental results in Gabra2 KO mice showing reduced direction selectivity in Off SACs and Off pathway responses.

claim: Lateral inhibition onto On SACs is not necessary for direction selectivity of the On pathway when the moving object is on a homogenous background.
source: In contrast, lateral inhibition onto On SACs is not necessary for direction selectivity of the On pathway when the moving object is on a homogenous background, but is required when the background is noisy.
evidence: This is demonstrated by calcium imaging and electrophysiology experiments showing normal On SAC direction selectivity in Gabra2 KO mice with simple moving bar stimuli.

claim: Lateral inhibition onto On SACs is required for direction selectivity when the background is noisy.
source: In contrast, lateral inhibition onto On SACs is not necessary for direction selectivity of the On pathway when the moving object is on a homogenous background, but is required when the background is noisy.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments showing impaired On pathway direction selectivity in Gabra2 KO mice when a flickering checkerboard background is used.

claim: Distinct sets of inhibitory mechanisms are recruited to generate direction selectivity under different visual conditions.
source: These results demonstrate that distinct sets of inhibitory mechanisms are recruited to generate direction selectivity under different visual conditions.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the differential effects observed in On vs Off pathways and with different stimulus conditions.

claim: Encoding of motion direction first appears in the inner plexiform layer (IPL) of mammalian retina.
source: Encoding of motion direction first appears in the inner plexiform layer (IPL) of mammalian retina (Barlow and Hill, 1963; Barlow and Levick, 1965; Oyster and Barlow, 1967), where positive- and negative-contrast motion stimuli are processed in anatomically distinct On and Off sublaminae.
evidence: This is supported by multiple classic citations in the field.

claim: Positive- and negative-contrast motion stimuli are processed in anatomically distinct On and Off sublaminae in the IPL.
source: Encoding of motion direction first appears in the inner plexiform layer (IPL) of mammalian retina (Barlow and Hill, 1963; Barlow and Levick, 1965; Oyster and Barlow, 1967), where positive- and negative-contrast motion stimuli are processed in anatomically distinct On and Off sublaminae.
evidence: This is established knowledge in retinal neuroscience supported by citations.

claim: On-Off DSGCs have bistratified dendritic arbors that receive directionally tuned inhibition from On and Off subtypes of SACs.
source: One of the main output neurons that signal motion direction from the retina to higher visual centers, the On-Off DSGC, has bistratified dendritic arbors that receive directionally tuned inhibition from On and Off subtypes of SACs at each of these sublamina (Figure 1A) (Famiglietti, 1983, 1992; Kittila and Massey, 1997; Taylor and Vaney, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: SACs are monostratified, axonless interneurons that release GABA and acetylcholine from varicosities at the distal ends of their dendritic arbors.
source: SACs are monostratified, axonless interneurons that release GABA and acetylcholine from varicosities at the distal ends of their dendritic arbors (Brecha et al., 1988; Famiglietti, 1991; Kosaka et al., 1988; O'Malley and Masland, 1989; Vaney and Young, 1988).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: GABAergic inputs preferentially originate from SAC dendritic sectors that extend in the anti-preferred (null) direction of On-Off DSGCs.
source: First, GABAergic inputs preferentially originate from SAC dendritic sectors that extend in the anti-preferred (null) direction of On-Off DSGCs (Figure 1B, Briggman et al., 2011; Fried et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2010; Wei et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: The dendritic sectors of SACs are electrotonically isolated and directionally tuned to motion in the centrifugal direction.
source: Second, the dendritic sectors of SACs are electrotonically isolated and directionally tuned to motion in the centrifugal direction (from soma to dendritic tips) (Figure 1B, Euler et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Euler et al., 2002 and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Maximal GABA release from SACs to DSGCs occurs during motion in the null direction.
source: Since null-direction motion for a DSGC corresponds to centrifugal motion for its presynaptic SAC dendrites, maximal GABA release from SACs to DSGCs occurs during motion in the null direction (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a logical inference from the spatial arrangement of SAC-DSGC connections and SAC directional tuning.

claim: SACs at each sublamina receive GABAergic lateral inhibition from neighboring SACs.
source: Along with providing inhibition to DSGCs, SACs at each sublamina receive GABAergic lateral inhibition from neighboring SACs (Ding et al., 2016; Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Lee and Zhou, 2006) and other wide-field amacrine cells (Ding et al., 2016; Lee and Zhou, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: SACs receive GABAergic lateral inhibition from other wide-field amacrine cells.
source: Along with providing inhibition to DSGCs, SACs at each sublamina receive GABAergic lateral inhibition from neighboring SACs (Ding et al., 2016; Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Lee and Zhou, 2006) and other wide-field amacrine cells (Ding et al., 2016; Lee and Zhou, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Reciprocal GABAergic inhibition between SACs is abolished in Slc32a1 KO mice.
source: We did not detect any evoked IPSCs in the KO group (Figure 1E, n = 9 pairs, three mice), indicating that reciprocal SAC-SAC inhibition is abolished in Slc32a1 KO mice.
evidence: This is demonstrated by paired recordings showing no evoked IPSCs in Slc32a1 KO mice.

claim: In control mice, reciprocal inhibition between SACs was detected in 9 out of 9 pairs with mean peak amplitude 16.4 ± 2.8 pA.
source: We detected reciprocal inhibition between SACs in 9 out of 9 pairs in the control group (Figure 1D, mean peak amplitude 16.4 ± 2.8 pA, five mice), consistent with previous studies (Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Lee and Zhou, 2006).
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from paired recordings.

claim: The leading edge of a bright bar evokes calcium transients in On SACs.
source: As expected, the leading edge of the bright bar evoked calcium transients in On SACs and the trailing edge evoked responses in Off SACs (Figure 2B, and Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 2B and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: The trailing edge of a bright bar evokes calcium transients in Off SACs.
source: As expected, the leading edge of the bright bar evoked calcium transients in On SACs and the trailing edge evoked responses in Off SACs (Figure 2B, and Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 2B and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: In control mice, dendritic calcium signals in both On and Off SACs show strong directional tuning to motion in the centrifugal direction.
source: In control mice, dendritic calcium signals in both On and Off SACs show strong directional tuning to motion in the centrifugal direction (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by calcium imaging data shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: In Slc32a1 KO mice, centrifugal direction selectivity of On SACs is similar to that of control mice.
source: In Slc32a1 KO mice, centrifugal direction selectivity (both DSI and vector sum) of On SACs is similar to that of control mice (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantitative analysis of calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Off SACs in Slc32a1 KO mice exhibit a small but statistically significant increase in DSI and vector sum values.
source: However, Off SACs exhibit a small, but statistically significant, increase in DSI and vector sum values (Figure 2F) due to decreased centripetal direction response (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The increased direction selectivity in Off SACs of Slc32a1 KO mice is due to decreased centripetal direction response.
source: However, Off SACs exhibit a small, but statistically significant, increase in DSI and vector sum values (Figure 2F) due to decreased centripetal direction response (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of response amplitudes shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Adding SR95531 to Slc32a1 KO retinas reduces direction selectivity parameters for both On and Off SACs.
source: Adding the GABAA receptor antagonist SR95531 to Slc32a1 KO retinas reduces these direction selectivity parameters for both On and Off SACs (Figure 2D–2G), indicating a role for GABAergic inhibition of SACs by non-SAC amacrine cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by pharmacological experiments shown in Figures 2D-2G.

claim: GABAergic inhibition of SACs by non-SAC amacrine cells plays a role in direction selectivity.
source: Adding the GABAA receptor antagonist SR95531 to Slc32a1 KO retinas reduces these direction selectivity parameters for both On and Off SACs (Figure 2D–2G), indicating a role for GABAergic inhibition of SACs by non-SAC amacrine cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the effect of SR95531 in Slc32a1 KO mice where SAC-SAC inhibition is already absent.

claim: For a simple moving bar stimulus, losing reciprocal SAC-SAC inhibition in Slc32a1 KO mice does not affect the direction selectivity of On SACs.
source: Our results demonstrate that, for a simple moving bar stimulus, losing reciprocal SAC-SAC inhibition in Slc32a1 KO mice does not affect the direction selectivity of On SACs, and enhances the direction selectivity of Off SACs.
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from the calcium imaging experiments in Slc32a1 KO mice.

claim: For a simple moving bar stimulus, losing reciprocal SAC-SAC inhibition in Slc32a1 KO mice enhances the direction selectivity of Off SACs.
source: Our results demonstrate that, for a simple moving bar stimulus, losing reciprocal SAC-SAC inhibition in Slc32a1 KO mice does not affect the direction selectivity of On SACs, and enhances the direction selectivity of Off SACs.
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from the calcium imaging experiments in Slc32a1 KO mice.

claim: Gabra2 expression colocalizes with On and Off SAC dendrites in the IPL.
source: Gabra2 expression colocalizes with On and Off SAC dendrites in the IPL (Brandstätter et al., 1995) and has been shown to be important for direction selectivity (Auferkorte et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Gabra2 has been shown to be important for direction selectivity.
source: Gabra2 expression colocalizes with On and Off SAC dendrites in the IPL (Brandstätter et al., 1995) and has been shown to be important for direction selectivity (Auferkorte et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Auferkorte et al., 2012.

claim: Spontaneous IPSCs in SACs are eliminated in Gabra2 KO mice.
source: To confirm loss of functional GABAA receptors in SACs of Gabra2 KO mice, we recorded their spontaneous IPSCs and found that they are eliminated (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: GABAergic inputs onto SACs are abolished in Gabra2 KO mice.
source: Therefore, GABAergic inputs onto SACs are abolished in Gabra2 KO mice.
evidence: This is concluded from the absence of spontaneous and evoked IPSCs in SACs of Gabra2 KO mice.

claim: In Gabra2 KO mice, the asymmetric wiring pattern of GABAergic inputs from SACs to pDSGCs remains unchanged.
source: In control mice, SACs from the null side provide strong GABAergic inputs onto pDSGCs while SACs from the preferred side provide weak GABAergic inputs. In Gabra2 KOs, this asymmetric wiring pattern remains unchanged (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by paired recording experiments shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: Cholinergic transmission from SACs to pDSGCs is unaffected in Gabra2 KO mice.
source: Similarly, cholinergic transmission in the KO is unaffected (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by paired recording experiments shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: The amplitude of EPSCs in pDSGCs evoked by a bright flashing spot is similar between control and Gabra2 KO groups.
source: In addition, the amplitude of EPSCs in pDSGCs evoked by a bright flashing spot is similar between control and Gabra2 KO groups (Figure 3G), indicating that both cholinergic and glutamatergic synapses onto pDSGCs are unaltered.
evidence: This is demonstrated by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Both cholinergic and glutamatergic synapses onto pDSGCs are unaltered in Gabra2 KO mice.
source: In addition, the amplitude of EPSCs in pDSGCs evoked by a bright flashing spot is similar between control and Gabra2 KO groups (Figure 3G), indicating that both cholinergic and glutamatergic synapses onto pDSGCs are unaltered.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar EPSC amplitudes in control and KO mice.

claim: Off SACs in Gabra2 KO mice display a significant increase in centripetal-direction response.
source: We found that Off SACs in these KOs display a significant increase in centripetal-direction response (Figure 4A and B, Video 3), resulting in reduced direction selectivity (Figure 4C–4F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by calcium imaging experiments shown in Figures 4A, 4B and Video 3.

claim: Off SACs in Gabra2 KO mice show reduced direction selectivity during the simple moving bar stimulus.
source: We found that Off SACs in these KOs display a significant increase in centripetal-direction response (Figure 4A and B, Video 3), resulting in reduced direction selectivity (Figure 4C–4F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantitative analysis shown in Figures 4C-4F.

claim: Direct GABAergic inputs onto Off SACs from non-SAC amacrine cells are important for centrifugal direction selectivity.
source: Therefore, direct GABAergic inputs onto Off SACs from non-SAC amacrine cells are important for centrifugal direction selectivity.
evidence: This is concluded from the reduced direction selectivity in Off SACs of Gabra2 KO mice.

claim: On SACs in Gabra2 KO mice exhibit centrifugal preference similar to those of control mice during the simple moving bar stimulus.
source: In contrast, we found that On SACs in the KOs exhibit centrifugal preference similar to those of control mice (Figure 4, Video 4), suggesting that direct GABAergic inputs are not required for direction selectivity in On SACs during the simple moving bar stimulus.
evidence: This is demonstrated by calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 4 and Video 4.

claim: Direct GABAergic inputs are not required for direction selectivity in On SACs during the simple moving bar stimulus.
source: In contrast, we found that On SACs in the KOs exhibit centrifugal preference similar to those of control mice (Figure 4, Video 4), suggesting that direct GABAergic inputs are not required for direction selectivity in On SACs during the simple moving bar stimulus.
evidence: This is inferred from the normal direction selectivity of On SACs in Gabra2 KO mice.

claim: Bath application of SR95531 reduced direction selectivity of On SACs in Gabra2 KO mice.
source: Bath application of SR95531 reduced direction selectivity of On SACs in KOs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting a role for presynaptic inhibition onto bipolar cells in generating direction selectivity.
evidence: This is demonstrated by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Presynaptic inhibition onto bipolar cells plays a role in generating direction selectivity in On SACs.
source: Bath application of SR95531 reduced direction selectivity of On SACs in KOs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting a role for presynaptic inhibition onto bipolar cells in generating direction selectivity.
evidence: This is inferred from the effect of SR95531 in Gabra2 KO mice where direct GABAergic inputs onto SACs are already absent.

claim: In control mice, both On and Off components of IPSCs in pDSGCs are direction selective.
source: In control mice, both On and Off components of IPSCs are direction selective (Figure 5A–5D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by voltage clamp recordings shown in Figures 5A-5D.

claim: In Gabra2 KO mice, the Off component of IPSCs in pDSGCs shows reduced selectivity.
source: In Gabra2 KO mice, the Off component of IPSCs shows reduced selectivity (Figure 5C and D) but the On component does not (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by voltage clamp recordings shown in Figures 5C and 5D.

claim: In Gabra2 KO mice, the On component of IPSCs in pDSGCs does not show reduced selectivity.
source: In Gabra2 KO mice, the Off component of IPSCs shows reduced selectivity (Figure 5C and D) but the On component does not (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by voltage clamp recordings shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: In the absence of GABAergic inputs onto SACs, the Off component of inhibitory inputs onto DSGCs displays impaired directional tuning.
source: Therefore, in the absence of GABAergic inputs onto SACs, the Off component of inhibitory inputs onto DSGCs displays impaired directional tuning.
evidence: This is concluded from the reduced direction selectivity of Off IPSCs in Gabra2 KO mice.

claim: The Off response of pDSGC spiking activity in Gabra2 KO mice shows less direction selectivity than that in control mice during the simple moving bar stimulus.
source: Consistent with the reduced directional tuning of IPSCs observed in the Off component, we found that the Off response of pDSGC spiking activity in Gabra2 KO mice shows less direction selectivity than that in control mice (Figure 6A and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by loose-patch recordings shown in Figures 6A and 6C.

claim: The On responses of pDSGCs in Gabra2 KO mice display direction selectivity similar to that of controls during the simple moving bar stimulus.
source: In contrast, the On responses in KOs display direction selectivity similar to that of controls (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by loose-patch recordings shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: Direction selectivity of the leading edge-evoked Off component in Gabra2 KOs was less than that in controls when using a dark bar against a bright background.
source: We found that direction selectivity of the leading edge-evoked Off component in Gabra2 KOs was again less than that in controls (Figure 6D and F), while the trailing edge-evoked On response of KOs shows direction selectivity similar to controls (Figure 6D and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by loose-patch recordings shown in Figures 6D and 6F.

claim: The trailing edge-evoked On response of pDSGCs in Gabra2 KOs shows direction selectivity similar to controls when using a dark bar against a bright background.
source: We found that direction selectivity of the leading edge-evoked Off component in Gabra2 KOs was again less than that in controls (Figure 6D and F), while the trailing edge-evoked On response of KOs shows direction selectivity similar to controls (Figure 6D and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by loose-patch recordings shown in Figures 6D and 6E.

claim: The Off component of pDSGC spiking activity becomes less directionally tuned in Gabra2 KO mice.
source: Therefore, the Off component of pDSGC spiking activity becomes less directionally tuned in Gabra2 KO mice.
evidence: This is concluded from the spiking recordings with both bright and dark moving bars.

claim: In control mice, the pDSGC spiking response maintains direction selectivity over a wide range of checker intensities.
source: In control mice, the pDSGC spiking response maintains direction selectivity over a wide range of checker intensities (Figure 7A–7C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by loose-patch recordings with flickering checkerboard backgrounds shown in Figures 7A-7C.

claim: The direction selectivity of the Off response in Gabra2 KO mice is reduced regardless of checker intensity.
source: Consistent with the earlier finding that lateral inhibition is crucial for direction selectivity of the Off component (Figure 6C and E), the direction selectivity of the Off response in Gabra2 KO mice is reduced regardless of checker intensity (Figure 7A and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by loose-patch recordings shown in Figures 7A and 7C.

claim: Replacing the gray background with a flickering checkerboard significantly reduces the On direction selectivity in Gabra2 KO mice.
source: Interestingly, however, replacing the gray background with a flickering checkerboard also significantly reduces the On direction selectivity in KO mice (Figure 7A and B), indicating a functional contribution of lateral inhibition during more complex stimuli.
evidence: This is demonstrated by loose-patch recordings shown in Figures 7A and 7B.

claim: Lateral inhibition makes a functional contribution to On pathway direction selectivity during more complex stimuli.
source: Interestingly, however, replacing the gray background with a flickering checkerboard also significantly reduces the On direction selectivity in KO mice (Figure 7A and B), indicating a functional contribution of lateral inhibition during more complex stimuli.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced On direction selectivity in Gabra2 KO mice with flickering checkerboard backgrounds.

claim: The On component of the pDSGC's spiking response displays normal direction selectivity at all illuminance and contrast levels tested in Gabra2 KO mice using the simple moving bar stimulus.
source: We found that, similar to the results with our original simple bar stimulus (Figure 6), the On component of the pDSGC's spiking response displays normal direction selectivity, while the Off component shows reduced direction selectivity at all illuminance and contrast levels tested (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by loose-patch recordings shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The Off component of the pDSGC's spiking response shows reduced direction selectivity at all illuminance and contrast levels tested in Gabra2 KO mice using the simple moving bar stimulus.
source: We found that, similar to the results with our original simple bar stimulus (Figure 6), the On component of the pDSGC's spiking response displays normal direction selectivity, while the Off component shows reduced direction selectivity at all illuminance and contrast levels tested (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by loose-patch recordings shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The impaired direction selectivity seen in the On pathway in Gabra2 KO mice with the flickering checkerboard background is not due to changes in stimulus contrast or ambient illuminance.
source: Therefore, the impaired direction selectivity seen in the On pathway in Gabra2 KO mice with the flickering checkboard background is not due to changes in stimulus contrast or ambient illuminance.
evidence: This is concluded from the experiments showing normal On direction selectivity at various contrast and illuminance levels with homogeneous backgrounds.

claim: The noise introduced by the flickering checkerboard is important for the functional recruitment of lateral inhibition in the On pathway.
source: Instead, the noise introduced by the flickering checkerboard is important for the functional recruitment of lateral inhibition in the On pathway.
evidence: This is concluded from the differential effects of flickering checkerboard vs. simple bar stimuli at matched contrast and illuminance levels.

claim: The optimal direction selectivity of a dark object, encoded by the Off pathway, requires lateral inhibition from non-SAC amacrine cells onto Off SACs.
source: The optimal direction selectivity of a dark object, encoded by the Off pathway, requires lateral inhibition from non-SAC amacrine cells onto Off SACs.
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the experiments with Off pathway responses in Gabra2 KO mice.

claim: Direction selectivity of a bright object, encoded by the On pathway, does not require lateral inhibition onto On SACs when the moving bar stimulus lies on a homogeneous background.
source: In contrast, direction selectivity of a bright object, encoded by the On pathway, does not require lateral inhibition onto On SACs when the moving bar stimulus lies on a homogeneous background, but does require it when the bar moves on a noisy background.
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the experiments with On pathway responses in Gabra2 KO mice under different stimulus conditions.

claim: Direction selectivity of a bright object, encoded by the On pathway, requires lateral inhibition onto On SACs when the bar moves on a noisy background.
source: In contrast, direction selectivity of a bright object, encoded by the On pathway, does not require lateral inhibition onto On SACs when the moving bar stimulus lies on a homogeneous background, but does require it when the bar moves on a noisy background.
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the experiments with On pathway responses in Gabra2 KO mice under different stimulus conditions.

claim: Slc32a1 KO and Gabra2 KO mice display no detectable developmental compensations in the direction selective circuit.
source: We found that these synapses showed no detectable changes (Pei et al., 2015) and Figure 3), indicating that removing GABA release or GABA receptors from SACs does not lead to compensatory developmental changes at other synapses in the direction selective circuit.
evidence: This is concluded from the examination of multiple synapse types in the direction selective circuit.

claim: The early development of retinal direction selectivity is highly resistant to changes in neural activity.
source: However, our findings are consistent with multiple previous studies that demonstrate that the early development of retinal direction selectivity is highly resistant to changes in neural activity (Chan and Chiao, 2008; Elstrott et al., 2008; Hamby et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2011; Wei et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Visual experience plays a role in refining the clustered distribution of preferred directions of On-Off DSGCs after direction selectivity is established.
source: After direction selectivity is established, visual experience has been shown to play a role in refining the clustered distribution of preferred directions of On-Off DSGCs (Bos et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bos et al., 2016.

claim: pDSGCs in both Slc32a1 KO and Gabra2 KO lines remain tuned to the posterior direction.
source: Furthermore, pDSGCs in both KO lines remain tuned to the posterior direction (Pei et al., 2015); data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiments.

claim: Under the simple bar stimulus condition, lateral inhibition is not necessary for centrifugal direction selectivity of On SACs.
source: However, when a bar moves against a homogeneous dark background, we found that blocking GABA release or GABA receptors of On SACs does not affect their centrifugal preference. Therefore, under this stimulus condition, lateral inhibition is not necessary for centrifugal direction selectivity of On SACs, and other mechanisms (Hausselt et al., 2007; Kim et al., 2014; Oesch and Taylor, 2010; Vlasits et al., 2016) must act to maintain it.
evidence: This is concluded from the experiments in Slc32a1 KO and Gabra2 KO mice with simple moving bar stimuli.

claim: The centrifugal preference of Off SAC dendrites requires GABAergic inputs onto Off SACs from non-SAC amacrine cells.
source: This indicates that the centrifugal preference of Off SAC dendrites requires additional GABAergic inputs onto Off SACs from non-SAC amacrine cells.
evidence: This is concluded from the differential effects in Slc32a1 KO vs Gabra2 KO mice.

claim: Wide-field amacrine cells synapse onto the proximal dendrites of Off SACs and contribute about 8% of the total number of inhibitory synapses onto Off SACs.
source: These cells are presumably the wide-field amacrine cells that synapse onto the proximal dendrites of Off SACs and contribute about 8% of the total number of inhibitory synapses onto Off SACs identified by connectomic reconstruction (Ding et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ding et al., 2016.

claim: The direction selective circuitry is not merely mirrored in the On and Off layers of the IPL, but consists of distinct sets of mechanisms in each sublamina.
source: Thus, the direction selective circuitry is not merely mirrored in the On and Off layers of the IPL, but consists of distinct sets of mechanisms in each sublamina.
evidence: This is concluded from the differential effects observed in On vs Off pathways in the KO mice.

claim: GABAergic inhibition onto SACs consists of multiple facets that are engaged differently during retinal processing of positive- and negative-contrast motion.
source: Moreover, our study shows that GABAergic inhibition onto SACs consists of multiple facets that are engaged differently during retinal processing of positive- and negative-contrast motion.
evidence: This is concluded from the differential effects observed with different stimulus contrasts and backgrounds.

claim: Lateral inhibition onto On SACs functions to safeguard direction selectivity against a noisy environment.
source: We postulate that lateral inhibition onto On SACs functions to safeguard direction selectivity against a noisy environment.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the differential effects of noisy vs homogeneous backgrounds.

claim: A noisy background increases activation of bipolar cells, which in turn provides stronger glutamatergic drive to the downstream amacrine cells including SACs.
source: A noisy background increases activation of bipolar cells, which in turn provides stronger glutamatergic drive to the downstream amacrine cells including SACs.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation proposed based on known circuit connectivity.

claim: Under noisy background conditions, the lateral inhibitory network may be in a more 'primed' state to be efficiently recruited by the motion stimuli and to exert its function.
source: Under this condition, the lateral inhibitory network may be in a more 'primed' state to be efficiently recruited by the motion stimuli and to exert its function.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the recruitment of lateral inhibition under noisy conditions.

claim: Amacrine cells involved in lateral inhibition are less activated when bipolar cells adapt to the gray background.
source: In contrast, amacrine cells involved in lateral inhibition are less activated when bipolar cells adapt to the gray background, and thus the moving bar alone may not be sufficient to significantly recruit lateral inhibition in the On pathway.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain why lateral inhibition is not recruited with homogeneous backgrounds.

claim: The moving bar alone may not be sufficient to significantly recruit lateral inhibition in the On pathway when bipolar cells adapt to a gray background.
source: In contrast, amacrine cells involved in lateral inhibition are less activated when bipolar cells adapt to the gray background, and thus the moving bar alone may not be sufficient to significantly recruit lateral inhibition in the On pathway.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the experimental observations.

claim: Additional neural mechanisms are recruited when the visual stimulus more closely resembles natural viewing conditions.
source: These findings represent an intriguing example in which additional neural mechanisms are recruited when the visual stimulus more closely resembles natural viewing conditions, but simpler visual stimuli involving only the feature of interest may not reveal the functional significance of these mechanisms (David et al., 2004; Felsen and Dan, 2005; Felsen et al., 2005; Turner and Rieke, 2016).
evidence: This is a general principle supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Simpler visual stimuli involving only the feature of interest may not reveal the functional significance of certain neural mechanisms.
source: These findings represent an intriguing example in which additional neural mechanisms are recruited when the visual stimulus more closely resembles natural viewing conditions, but simpler visual stimuli involving only the feature of interest may not reveal the functional significance of these mechanisms (David et al., 2004; Felsen and Dan, 2005; Felsen et al., 2005; Turner and Rieke, 2016).
evidence: This is a general principle supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A prominent inhibitory component in the receptive field of visual cortical neurons is uniquely revealed by more complex natural stimuli but is not observed with synthetic sinusoidal gratings.
source: A notable analogy has been reported in the visual cortex: a prominent inhibitory component in the receptive field of visual cortical neurons is uniquely revealed by more complex natural stimuli but is not observed with synthetic sinusoidal gratings (David et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to David et al., 2004.

claim: The effect of GABAA receptor antagonist SR95531 cannot be attributed to specific type(s) of GABAergic synapses since GABAA receptors are extensively expressed in amacrine cells and bipolar cells in the IPL.
source: Furthermore, the effect of the antagonist cannot be attributed to specific type(s) of GABAergic synapses since GABAA receptors are extensively expressed in amacrine cells and bipolar cells in the IPL.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitation of pharmacological approaches based on known receptor expression patterns.

claim: Combining pharmacology with genetic dissection of the GABAergic circuitry allows determination of the synaptic loci that participate in direction selectivity.
source: Here, we combined pharmacology with the genetic dissection of the GABAergic circuitry to determine the synaptic loci that participate in direction selectivity.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach used in the study.
